question.text: If the activation energy of a reaction is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>80</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>9</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kJ</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, the fraction of molecules at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>700</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math>, having enough energy to react to form products is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></mrow></msup></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></math> is (Rounded off to the nearest integer) [Use <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>31</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>]

solution.text:
Fraction of molecules to have enough energy to react =e-Ea/RT

So, x=EaRT

=80.9×1038.31×700

=13.9≈14
